title: The Most Valuable Thing (Português)
summary: Akbar asks his ministers to name the most valuable commodity in existence. Birbal names the one treasure that even emperors cannot purchase. [PT]
full_text:
During a discussion in the Diwan-i-Khas regarding the imperial trade monopolies, Emperor Akbar asked his ministers:

'What is the single most valuable, indispensable commodity in all the markets of the world? Is it gold, water, grain, or iron?'

The finance minister replied: 'Gold, Sire! For with gold, one can purchase armies, cities, and palaces.'

The general argued: 'Iron! For without iron swords and plows, gold is easily stolen and crops cannot be harvested.'

A physician suggested: 'Water and air! For without them, no living soul can survive for three days.'

Birbal stood up and said with profound solemnity:

'Sire, all those things are valuable, yet if you lose gold, you can earn it back. If an iron blade is broken, it can be reforged. If water dries up, the rains will fall again next season.

'The most valuable, irreplaceable thing in the universe is Time.'

Akbar leaned forward: 'Explain yourself, Birbal.'

Birbal said: 'Consider this, Your Majesty. You possess an imperial treasury overflowing with ten million gold mohurs and mountains of diamonds.

'Yet if you were lying upon your deathbed, and offered every single coin, diamond, palace, and province in your vast empire to purchase back just one single hour of yesterday—could all your wealth buy back sixty lost seconds?

'No emperor, no conqueror, no sage can ever reclaim a moment that has slipped past. The minutes we waste in idle gossip, petty quarrels, and unrighteous anger are lost forever into eternity. Therefore, Time is the supreme treasure of human life.'

Akbar fell silent in deep contemplation. He thanked Birbal for the profound reminder, and resolved to dedicate every hour of his reign to the diligent service of his people.
